subject: mathematics
question_text: If f: R→R and g: R→R are defined by f(x) = 4x − 1 and g(x) = x² + 2, find (gof)((a + 1)/4).

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.10, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 12(ii). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split rewards the inner value f((a + 1)/4) = a first and the outer value g(a) = a² + 2 second. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find (gof)((a + 1)/4) — which function acts first, and the value you reach.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Apply f first
steps.margin_note: First mark. In gof the function written on the right, f, acts first, so (a + 1)/4 goes into f before g is used.

recall.must_convey: That f acts first on (a + 1)/4, the two 4s cancel, and f((a + 1)/4) = a.
accept: in g o f the function f acts first so put a plus one by four into f
four times a plus one by four is a plus one and minus one gives a
the fours cancel so f of that input is a
modata f apply cheyyali so answer a vastundi
f of a plus one over four equals a

steps.why: In gof the function on the right acts first. Here the 4 in f(x) = 4x − 1 cancels the 4 in the denominator, so the input handed to g is simply a.
steps.memory_tip: In gof, f is the inner function. Work f first, and the 4 outside cancels the 4 in the denominator.
common_mistakes: Applying g first, which computes fog and gives a different expression.
Cancelling only the 4 and writing a + 1 instead of a.

steps.label: Apply g to that output
steps.margin_note: Second mark. g receives a, not (a + 1)/4. Put a into x² + 2 and write the single expression.

recall.must_convey: That g is applied to a, giving a² + 2.
accept: then g of a is a squared plus two
put a into x squared plus two and get a squared plus two
the answer is a squared plus two
g lo a pettite a square plus two vastundi
g receives a so the value is a squared plus two

steps.why: The outer function acts on the OUTPUT of f, which is a. Writing g(a) shows that (a + 1)/4 is never put into g.
steps.memory_tip: The outer function receives f's output, not the original input. Here that output is a.
common_mistakes: Writing g((a + 1)/4) instead of g(a) at the last step.
Expanding (4x − 1)² + 2 in x and then forgetting to put x = (a + 1)/4.
